evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'No Protection' (released 17 February 1995; Wild Bunch/Circa, per The Guardian's review) says Massive Attack first asked Mad Professor for a single remix after 'Protection' came out, then asked him to listen to more of the album with a view to further remixes, which became the whole record. It describes his treatment as heavily edited into a slow, pulsating mix with the beat emphasised, extensive reverb, and vocals fading in and out in dub fashion. Wikipedia's Massive Attack article dates the band's formation to 1988 in Bristol, out of the Wild Bunch sound system.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Play a track from 'Protection' and then its twin on 'No Protection'. The dub version slows the feel down and pushes the beat forward, drenches everything in reverb, and lets the voices drift in and out rather than carrying the song. It is the same move Tubby made on Kingston singles, applied to a Bristol album twenty years later.

explanation: Massive Attack asked Mad Professor to remix one song from their album 'Protection'. They liked it enough to ask him to keep going, and he remade the whole album as dub, released in 1995 as 'No Protection'. It is a documented commission, not a likeness: the band invited a second-generation dub engineer to rebuild their album the Kingston way. It closes a loop, since Massive Attack themselves came out of a UK sound system, a practice that began in Jamaica.
